An air vessel is used in a reciprocating pump

options.html: to obtain continuous supply of the fluid.

questions.solution:
(d)
An air vessel in a reciprocating pump acts as a buffer or reservoir, which helps in smoothing out
the flow rate and pressure variations caused by the piston's reciprocating motion. During the
pump's stroke when flow is high, excess liquid enters the air vessel and compresses the air inside.
When the flow is low, the compressed air expands and pushes liquid back into the pipe. This
process maintains a nearly uniform flow rate and provides a continuous supply of the fluid. This
also leads to other benefits such as reduced acceleration head, lower frictional losses, and the
ability to run the pump at higher speeds.

Crippling and web buckling may be prevented by
1. increasing the length of bearing plate.
2. decreasing the length of bearing plate.
3. increasing the thickness of the web.
4. decreasing the thickness of the web.
Of these, the correct statements are:
questions.solution:
(a)
• Increasing the length of bearing plate: Web crippling is a local failure caused by excessive bearing stress under a concentrated load. By increasing the length of the bearing plate, the concentrated load is distributed over a larger area, which reduces the bearing stress and helps prevent crippling.
• Increasing the thickness of the web: Web buckling is a failure of the web under diagonal compressive stresses. A thicker web increases the stiffness and resistance to this type of buckling. Similar to how a thicker column is more resistant to buckling.

questions.solution:

Type III or "hindered settling" because the high concentration of particles creates resistance to

Consider two traditional composting methods. Method A and method B. Method A involves decomposition in sealed pits or trenches, limiting oxygen supply. Method B involves organic matter piled in heaps and periodically turned over to ensure aeration

options.html: Method A is the Indore method (aerobic), and Method B is the Bangalore method (anaerobic).
Method A is the Bangalore method (anaerobic), and method B is the indore method (aerobic)
Both method A and method B are aerobic processes, representing variations of the Indore method
Both method A and method B are anaerobic processes, representing variations of the Bangalore method.

questions.solution:
(b)
1. Method A (sealed pits, limited oxygen): The description of decomposing waste in sealed pits without aeration perfectly matches the characteristics of the Bangalore method. This method relies on anaerobic microorganisms to break down the complex organic matter into simpler substances.
2. Method B (piled heaps, turned periodically, aeration): The description of composting in piles with regular turning for aeration perfectly matches the characteristics of the Indore method.
This method relies on aerobic microorganisms, which require oxygen to decompose materials efficiently and quickly.

questions.html: In surveying and civil engineering projects, what is the primary purpose of combining the data obtained from both profile leveling and cross-sectioning?

options.html: To determine the precise atmospheric pressure changes along the survey route.
The establish the horizontal alignment (layout of the project's centre line).
To accurately calculate the volume of earthwork (cut and fill) required for construction
To measure the magnetic bearing and inclination of the land being surveyed

questions.solution:
(c)
• Profile levelling provides the vertical data (elevations) along the center line, which determines the depth of cut or the height of fill needed at different points.
• Cross-sectioning provides the necessary data to determine the area of the earthwork section of vanous intervals along the route
By combining the areas from the cross-sections with the distances between them (derived from
the profile and plan view), engineers can calculate the precise volumes of material that must be
excavated (cut) or added (fill) to achieve the final desired ground level or formation level. This
process is fundamental for efficient and cost-effective earthwork construction

Which of the following conditions a good tongue rail should satisfy?
1. The top and sides of a tongue rail are tapered in such a way that it does not bear any load.
2. The tongue rail should be some what (about 6 mm) higher than the stock rail at the centre.
questions.solution:
(c)
• Tapered Design: A good tongue rail is tapered to fit closely against the stock rail. The tapering on the top and sides is crucial to ensure that the wheel's load is transferred to the full rail section after the switch, preventing damage to the switch mechanism.
• Height Difference: In a specific design known as an overriding switch, which is standardized on the Indian Railways, the head of the tongue rail is intentionally kept approximately 6 mm higher than the stock rail for part of its length. This design feature helps to reduce the amount of undercut needed in the foot of the tongue rail and eliminates the possibility of splitting if a false flange moves in the trailing direction.

3. Drainage and water management systems can be simpler and more effectively designed.

questions.solution:
(a)
Construction costs are generally higher for twin tunnels than for a single-bore tunnels because two separate structures need to be excavated and built. The other advantages (safety, ventilation, etc.) are often seen as justifying this increased initial cost.

Statement (I): For a section having an axis of symmetry there will not be twisting if the loading axis coincides with the symmetrical axis.
Statement (II): The plane of loading contains the bending axis.
questions.solution:
(c)
For bending without twisting, plane of loading must contain one of the principal central axis of
the section. In case the section is having a plane of symmetry, the symmetrical plane contains the
principal central axis. Thus statement (I) is correct. The bending axis is perpendicular to the plane
of loading and hence statement (II) is wrong.
